title: Context Weaver — node descriptions
description: The semantic layer of the knowledge graph. Written by the Architect agent (or by generate-descriptions.js) to .github/.pipeline-context/context/descriptions.json after reading the authoring brief, then loaded onto Neo4j nodes by Graph Forge. Everything here is INTERPRETATION, not parser output — downstream agents treat it as orienting context to be verified against source, never as evidence in its own right.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when these descriptions were written.

artifactsGeneratedAt.description: Copy of `artifactsGeneratedAt` from the workload file. Ties this description set to the scan it was written against.

author.description: Who wrote these. Use `architect-agent` when the agent authored them in-context, or `llm:<model-id>` (e.g. `llm:claude-opus-5`) when generate-descriptions.js did. Stored on every node so a consumer knows the provenance.

nodes.description: One entry per described node. Nodes may be omitted — a missing description is a smaller problem than a wrong one.

kind.description: Neo4j label this description attaches to. Copy verbatim from the workload.

id.description: The node's key, copied verbatim from the workload: Module/Package/ExternalType use `name`, Type uses the FQN, Method uses `TypeId#name(paramTypes)`, Endpoint uses `METHOD /path`. A value that matches no node in artifacts.json is a validation error.

fingerprint.description: Copied verbatim from the workload. Records which shape of the code this description was written against, so a later scan can mark it stale instead of serving a description that has silently become false.

summary.description: 1-3 sentences: what this is and what it is for, in the language of the domain rather than the language of the code. Say what a reader could not get from the signature. Bad: 'A service class with three methods.' Good: 'Owns the employee roster and is the only writer of the employees Mongo collection; every other service reads employees through its REST surface.'

role.description: Short architectural role label, used for filtering and grouping. Suggested values: controller, service, repository, entity, dto, configuration, client, scheduler, exception, mapper, util, bootstrap, discovery, gateway, contract, framework-base, layer, deployable.

responsibilities.description: The distinct jobs this node owns, one per entry. Keep to what it actually does, not what its name suggests.

criticality.description: How much damage a defect here does — not how complex the code is. `critical` means an outage or data loss across services; `low` means a contained, cosmetic, or easily-noticed failure. Blast Radius uses this to rank impact.

sideEffects.description: Observable effects beyond returning a value: database writes, outbound HTTP calls, message publishes, cache mutation, file or config writes, scheduled triggers. This is the primary input to blast-radius reasoning — an empty array means genuinely pure, not merely unknown.

invariants.description: What must hold true for this to be correct — required ordering, non-null guarantees, uniqueness, idempotency, transaction boundaries, expected value ranges. A violated invariant is usually the root cause, so state them even when they look obvious.

failureModes.description: How this realistically breaks and what the caller sees when it does — 'returns an empty list instead of 404 when the id is unknown', 'silently drops the update when the collection is missing'. Written for a Root Cause agent triaging a symptom.

dataTouched.description: Named collections, tables, entities, config keys, or topics this reads or writes. Prefix with `reads:` / `writes:` where the distinction matters.

upstream.description: Who or what drives this — callers, schedules, external services, user actions. Include callers the Java call graph cannot see, such as cross-service HTTP consumers.

downstream.description: What this depends on to do its job — services, datastores, config sources, third-party APIs.

testHints.description: Concrete ways to exercise this: the request to replay, the fixture the test needs, the boundary condition worth asserting, the collaborator worth stubbing. Written for the QA agent building a test plan.

confidence.description: `high` only when the source and its collaborators make the intent unambiguous. `low` when this is a plausible reading that a reader should verify before acting on it. Downstream agents weight claims by this — an honest `low` is more useful than a confident guess.

evidence.description: Where the claims came from: `path/to/File.java:42`, an annotation, a pom dependency. Lets a reader check the description instead of trusting it.

openQuestions.description: What the source could not settle. Use this instead of guessing — an explicit unknown is a lead for the next agent.

crossCutting.description: Facts that belong to no single node: shared datastores, service-to-service dependencies that carry no Java call edge, deployment ordering, environment coupling. Loaded as `:ContextNote` nodes linked by `[:ABOUT]` to everything they concern.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, e.g. `shared-employee-collection`. Re-using it on a later run updates the note rather than duplicating it.

text.description: The fact and why it matters, in 1-3 sentences.

modules.description: Module names this note concerns. Must exist in artifacts.json.

types.description: Fully-qualified type ids this note concerns. Must exist in artifacts.json.
